title: Operational definition
statement: An operational definition states how a construct or quantity is observed, measured, classified, or manipulated so that evidence can be interpreted and procedures can be examined or repeated.
limitations: An operational definition can be precise yet still fail to capture the intended construct or support external validity.

title: Reproducibility and replicability
statement: Reproducibility commonly concerns obtaining consistent computational results from the same data, code, methods, and conditions, while replicability concerns obtaining consistent evidence from a new study addressing the same question.
limitations: Terminology varies across disciplines, so every project should declare the meaning and conditions it is testing.

title: Uncertainty belongs with an estimate
statement: A quantitative estimate should be accompanied by the assumptions, sampling or measurement basis, and an appropriate account of uncertainty rather than presented as an exact context-free fact.
limitations: No single uncertainty summary captures every source of model, measurement, and decision uncertainty.
